s: a former cordonnerie turned tiny coffee sanctuary
w: A former shoe-repair workshop on a narrow northern Marais street, its blue facade still lettered "cordonnerie" from its past life. Now one of Paris's smallest specialty coffee spots -- white tiles, vintage fittings, barely room for a handful inside plus a couple of stools out front. A quiet, stolen-cup kind of place rather than a destination café.
_facts: Located at 19 Rue du Pont aux Choux, 75003 Paris, in the northern Marais
Housed in a former cordonnerie (shoe-repair workshop), whose signage remains on the facade
Extremely small specialty coffee bar with minimal indoor seating
Opened in the 2010s as part of Paris's third-wave coffee expansion into the Marais

s: a 1915 corner café revived by the Belleville Brûlerie roasters
w: A classic corner café in a 1915 building between Canal Saint-Martin and Belleville, taken over and revived by the team behind the nearby Belleville Brûlerie roastery. Terrace life runs from quiet mornings into afternoon bustle, with roasted-round-the-corner coffee and the kind of unhurried, regulars-only rhythm that stays off the main tourist circuits.
_facts: Located at 31-33 Rue Juliette Dodu, 75010 Paris, between Canal Saint-Martin and Belleville
Building dates from 1915; the café was revived by La Brûlerie de Belleville, a Paris specialty roaster
Known for its terrace and neighbourhood, regulars-driven atmosphere
Serves coffee roasted by the affiliated Belleville roastery

s: a quiet neighbourhood roastery-café steps from the plant-lined Rue des Thermopyles
w: A low-key roastery-café in the residential 14th arrondissement, a few steps from the car-free, plant-crowded cobbles of Rue des Thermopyles. No pretence, just steady local trade throughout the day -- the kind of everyday find that only turns up by wandering off the main boulevards.
_facts: Located at 121 Rue du Château, 75014 Paris
A short walk from Rue des Thermopyles, a car-free, plant-lined residential street
